consolidated_key_facts: Cell membrane disruption drugs work by forming pores on the nanometer scale, leading to membrane depolarization and leakage of ions and metabolites.
The mechanism typically involves attraction of the drug (AP) to the membrane, attachment, and subsequent insertion into the membrane to cause disruption.
